0.label: plaited_interlace_field
0.description: A square field of broad, grooved strands woven over and under in a diagonal plait, second compartment from the top of the plank.
0.iconography: Mat or basket weaving rendered in wood — the plait that frames and divides Ife-area carving. It separates the incised sign above from the figure below.

1.label: spiral_pierced_by_rod
1.description: A large spiral of about nine coils with a straight rod driven diagonally into its centre, filling the lowest compartment of the plank.
1.iconography: A coiled serpent (or snail) run through by a spear or staff — a coil-and-rod emblem that also appears as a ring-and-rod on the Ado-Ekiti door (EBA-Div_00303 #18). The coil fits the project's ouroboros / renewal family; the rod may mark its conquest or binding. The coil count invites a number reading but is untested.

2.label: incised_cross_sign
2.description: A shallow incised sign at the very top of the plank: a cross whose arms end in angled brackets, like a four-pointed star.
2.iconography: Not a picture but a sign, closer to a mark or glyph — comparable to the geometric signs of àrokò messages or to owners' and makers' marks. Its meaning is unknown.

3.label: figure_holding_two_staffs
3.description: A frontal standing figure with a large round head marked by a central ridge, a beaded belt, holding a tall staff upright in each hand, filling the plank's central compartment.
3.iconography: Holding two staffs of office marks a ruler, chief or priest; the figure is the plank's protagonist. In a chronicle reading, the principal person of this plank.

4.label: kneeling_offering_figures
4.description: Two small figures in the left third of the narrow register below the main figure: one kneeling and raising an object, one seated.
4.iconography: Kneeling with raised hands is offering or greeting before a person of rank — here, the figure above.

5.label: displayed_figure_w_legs
5.description: A small figure in the centre of the lower narrow register, arms raised to the head and legs drawn as a looped 'W'.
5.iconography: A displayed pose, arms up and legs spread — linked in Yoruba carving to birth, fertility and invocation. The looped legs also recall the mudfish-legged figures of Olókun and the Benin king.

6.label: figure_with_raised_arm
6.description: A narrow, partly cut figure at the right end of the lower register, one arm raised.
6.iconography: A third attendant in the small register; too fragmentary to read further.

panel.title: Ife plank: sign, plait, staff-holder, attendants and pierced spiral
panel.object_type: carved plank (door leaf or post face)
panel.summary: A narrow plank photographed at an angle, carved in stacked compartments from top to bottom: an incised cross-sign, a plaited field, a figure holding two staffs, a row of small attendants and a large spiral pierced by a rod.

register_readings.reading: An incised four-pointed cross — a sign rather than an image.
A plaited field separating the sign from the figure.
The protagonist: a frontal figure holding a staff in each hand.
Small attendants below him: kneeling offerers and a displayed figure.
A nine-coil spiral pierced by a rod — serpent or snail, bound or speared.

panel.composition: A single vertical column of framed compartments; scale ranks the staff-holder above his small attendants, and the two abstract compartments (plait, spiral) bracket the figures.
panel.narrative: Read top to bottom, the plank sets a person of authority — two staffs, attendants kneeling before him — between a woven field and a pierced coil. If the coil is a serpent, the plank may pair a ruler with an emblem of renewal or conquered danger; the incised sign at the top reads like a label or mark. Taken with its sister planks from the same plate, it belongs to a sequence of framed personages.
panel.hypotheses: Some support for 'chronicle': a single ranked personage with attendants, one of several on the plate. The nine-coil spiral and plait are candidates for 'pattern as number' but nothing yet links them to a count.
cross_panel_links: Its sister planks EBA-Div_00311 panels 01 and 02 come from the same photograph.
The coil-and-rod echoes the ring-and-rod emblem on the Ado-Ekiti door (EBA-Div_00303 #18).
The plaited field is the same idiom that frames FoA_04-5578 and EBA-Div_00312.
uncertainties: The rod through the spiral could be a crack in the wood.
#4-#6 split one row of small figures into three boxes.
